Pass 4 — the mobile white line and the dusk-shrine score
summary: Two complaints drove this pass: an unwanted white line in the mobile layout, and a requested calmer, Dark Souls-flavoured soundtrack. (1) White line: a mobile probe (iPhone-class Chrome, 360/390/414 px, rest+play states, DOM light-element sweep + geometry reads) found exactly one pure-white painted element — the dusk dial's <input type=range>, whose UA widget paints a white background box and pale track reading as a light line in the dark dial. Fixed by hand-theming the slider (appearance:none, 4px dark track, amber fill via --ef-dial-fill set by DuskDial on mount/poll/drag, amber knob, -moz variants); sweep is now clean at all three widths. (2) Score: replaced the wind/crickets/owl bedscape with web/lib/music.ts (delegated design, integrated by hand) — a procedural D-aeolian 'dusk shrine' loop: breathing D2+A2 drone, slow open-fifth/add9 pad swells, sparse bell-like D-minor-pentatonic+dorian melody, rare chime, runtime-built convolution reverb, one 38.4s cycle scheduled by a single lookahead timer with tails ringing across the boundary (seamless loop); MUSIC_LEVEL 0.16 leaves footstep/master headroom. ambience.ts now hosts only the shared context, mute/dim ramps and footstep synth. Also: browser-smoke navigation wait moved off networkidle0 (Vite HMR socket never settles it); new music-probe harness. Verified: typecheck, build, forest.check(27), browser-smoke(12), mobile sweep clean, music probe (28 voices, running, envelopes complete, no errors).

title: Pass 5 — the score, audible
summary: User report: the new score is barely hearable. Root causes: MUSIC_LEVEL 0.16 sat far too low for sparse sine/triangle content, and the drone's D2/A2 fundamentals (73-110 Hz) fall below what phone speakers reproduce. Raised MUSIC_LEVEL to 0.42 (+8.4 dB overall), NOTE_LEVEL to 0.22 and PAD_LEVEL to 0.16 (signature layers up relative), and added a quiet D3 octave partial (DRONE_OCTAVE_LEVEL 0.3, breathing with the drone LFO) so the floor registers on small drivers. Worst-case coinciding peak now ~0.32 full scale into destination (was ~0.12), footsteps still keep headroom. Verified: typecheck clean, music probe (29 voices, context running, envelopes complete, no errors). Ear-tuning knobs remain the named constants atop web/lib/music.ts.

Pass 8 — solid tree trunks (collision) integrated from a chat-model brief
summary: Task 1 of the owner's three-task card (collision / dial lag / night visibility). Trees were pure visuals: the rig integrated velocity with only the soft PLAY_RADIUS boundary, so the walker clipped straight through trunks. Design: analytics in a pure leaf module rather than a physics engine — the deterministic scatter (collectSpots, seed evening-forest/trees/v1) moved VERBATIM from web/scene/Trees.tsx into new web/lib/tree-field.ts so renderer and collision share one source of truth; per-tree trunk colliders r = 0.18 + 0.22 * effectiveScale (broadleaf amber 1.08 bump mirrors the rendered matrix; contact distance r + PLAYER_RADIUS 0.3 = 0.66-0.80 m, the owner's chosen 'medium' feel); createTreeField() adds a cell-size-8 spatial hash with a 3x3 neighbourhood near() query. The rig (FirstPersonRig) now pushes the camera out of overlapping trunk circles after integration and cancels only the inward velocity component — slide, no bounce, no hard stop. Spawn safety holds (MIN_RADIUS 11 vs walker at r 10). New forest.check section: determinism (count + element-wise), radii bounds, grid-vs-brute-force over 200 seeded samples incl. negative cells, walker-start clearance. Note: tree-field.ts is the first pure lib module importing sibling lib modules, so its relative imports carry explicit .ts extensions (node strip-types requires them; shell tsconfig allowImportingTsExtensions allows them). QUALITY GATE: tsc clean, vite build green, forest.check all-pass incl. 5 new checks; browser smoke + visual probe SKIP — no Chrome binary on this machine (puppeteer-core candidates + empty ms-playwright cache). title: Pass 9 — dusk dial drag unstalled (touch-action + pointer-gated poll)
summary: Task 2 of three. The value pipeline was already instant (onChange -> shared timeOfDay.value -> per-frame DaylightDriver), so the reported lag was native-gesture: (1) .evening-forest-stage's touch-action:none (needed for game look-drag) leaked into the menu slider, and iOS/WebKit refuses to drag a range thumb under it — fixed with touch-action:auto scoped to .evening-forest-dial input[type=range] only; (2) the 250ms poll wrote el.value/applyFill whenever document.activeElement !== el, which does not reliably hold during touch drags, so the poll could fight the gesture — replaced by a real draggingRef gate: onPointerDown sets it, window-level pointerup/pointercancel clear it (pointer capture can retarget the release), and the poll skips both writes while dragging (label keeps refreshing; onChange keeps fill+label live mid-drag). [ / ] keyboard nudges still sync through the poll when the menu is open. Integrated verbatim from the chat-model response. QUALITY GATE: tsc clean, vite build green, forest.check all-pass; browser smoke/probe still skip (no Chrome on this machine — real-device check pending owner).

summary: Owner verdict after testing 9fbe821: keep ONLY task 1 (solid tree trunks). Tasks 2 (dusk-dial drag fix) and 3 (moonlit night) are backed out — DuskDial.tsx, evening-forest.css, daylight.ts, clock.ts, DaylightDriver.tsx, RetroEffects.tsx restored to the 7c88f34 state; forest.check.ts and README.md re-applied with the tree-field additions only. Reason given with the revert request: 'when you change the time of day it chooses automatically and starts — i want confirmation so the user knows what the toggle means; on mobile it is ok (tap to step into the trees)'. Diagnosis for the follow-up pass: on desktop drei's PointerLockControls installs a document-wide click handler that calls controls.lock(), so ANY click in the rest menu (dial included) enters the forest — touch devices never mount it, which is exactly why mobile feels correct. Candidate fix: scope the click-to-lock selector to the canvas host so entering requires the explicit button, plus a confirm step for dial changes. summary: Follow-up to n25's diagnosis, owner-approved ('Fix now', 'preview is enough' — no extra apply button): drei's PointerLockControls without a selector prop attaches its click-to-lock handler to document, so on desktop ANY click in the rest menu — dusk dial included — locked the pointer and started the forest; touch devices never mount the control, which is why mobile felt correct ('tap to step into the trees'). Dial drag is now purely a live lighting preview in the menu, on every device. Verified the installed drei implements selector as document.querySelectorAll(selector) with [document] fallback.
